headline: High-risk file and API interaction: ms-swift can read/write local artifacts and call external model APIs, while ComfyUI is offline-only but can still be fed into ms-swift workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP/browser bridge, so direct injection into it is limited. ms-swift can read files and use stdin/stdout, so if ComfyUI outputs are manually copied or written into shared files, prompt-like content could influence ms-swift. The pathway is possible but not default and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text into ms-swift prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file is used as an instruction channel between the agents, ms-swift may follow attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste generated content into ms-swift prompts without review.
Use a strict prompt template for ms-swift inputs.
Rename shared files to data-only conventions and strip instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any handoff artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, seeds, checkpoints, and other local artifacts, while ms-swift can read the filesystem and also sends data to external model APIs. If they share a workspace, ms-swift can ingest ComfyUI artifacts and transmit them onward, creating a default-unsafe leakage path for sensitive local data.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory tree, ms-swift can read ComfyUI artifacts.
IF sensitive images or checkpoints are present in that tree, they can flow to allowlisted external APIs via ms-swift.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Restrict ms-swift to a narrow input folder.
Remove sensitive files from shared paths before running ms-swift.
Disable outbound API calls for jobs that touch private artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-job data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI does not write the filesystem, but ms-swift does, so they can conflict over shared mutable files such as configs, logs, checkpoints, or training outputs if placed in the same workspace. The profiles do not state locking or shared-state isolation, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF ms-swift writes logs or outputs while ComfyUI reads adjacent artifacts, race conditions may corrupt work products.
mitigations: Use separate output directories.
Run only one writer per directory.
Make shared paths read-only for ComfyUI.
Back up checkpoints before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows, images, and model artifacts that ms-swift may consume as inputs, and ms-swift can then act on them through CLI/Python/API flows. There is no documented verification step between them, so errors or hallucinated metadata from ComfyUI can cascade into ms-swift processing or evaluation.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are used as authoritative inputs to ms-swift, downstream errors can propagate.
IF ms-swift automates evaluation or training from those outputs, incorrect artifacts can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Validate file formats before handoff.
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline.
Limit ms-swift to read-only evaluation on ComfyUI artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff files.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-only and does not request secrets, while ms-swift handles hub/sdk tokens and can call external APIs. If regulated or private data from ComfyUI is processed by ms-swift, the compliance burden shifts to the external services and token-handling path. The profiles do not prove a residency violation, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF private or regulated data from ComfyUI is passed into ms-swift jobs, external processing obligations apply.
IF the operator uses ms-swift with tokens against third-party endpoints, retention and residency must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ms-swift runs.
Rotate and scope tokens before use.
Review vendor retention terms for each API.
Log which datasets were sent externally.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
